summary: Redwood AE + SE (Samir, Jin) ran a security/compliance and integration review with ClearHealth security and platform team. Primary focuses: SSO via SAML, SCIM provisioning for user groups, RBAC/least-privilege model, audit logs and retention, KMS/encryption and data residency considerations. Agreed to run a short RBAC workshop and provision a test tenant for an IdP handshake; Redwood to share SAML metadata, SCIM docs, SOC 2/ISO artifacts and example role policies. Customer raised questions on scoped service principals, read-only vs admin roles, deletion/disable flow for SCIM, and audit log retention windows for compliance. No blockers; timeline is a short pilot over next two weeks.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: hi everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick agenda runthrough, i'm samir from redwood inference, i'm the AE on the account. jin is our solutions engineer.

[00:18] Laura Mitchell: hey hi thanks, from clearhealth here, laura mitchell, head of security. we have tom and anika on as well.

[00:26] Jin Park: hey all, quick note — we're going to focus on SSO and SCIM flows and then RBAC. feel free to interrupt with compliance Qs.

[00:35] Tom Reyes: great thanks. our main ask is we need SAML SSO into your console and SCIM provisioning so we can automate offboarding. also need audit logs for SOC 2.

[00:45] Samir Patel: sounds good. quick Q: are you using okta as your IdP now?

[00:50] Laura Mitchell: yes okta for prod; dev uses a mix but prod is okta, and we also have auth0 for a couple of small apps.

[00:58] Jin Park: perfect. redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM v2 for provisioning. we can provide service provider (SP) metadata, certificate, endpoints. provisioning supports create/update/deactivate flows.

[01:15] Laura Mitchell: on deprovisioning — we need immediate deactivation and a soft-delete audit so we can prove access was removed. how quick is the SCIM deprovision?

[01:25] Jin Park: SCIM calls are near-real time; when your IdP sends a deprovision action we deactivate in seconds, we also log the event to the audit stream. small caveat — if you use deferred provisioning or a cache TTL it could be slightly delayed, but standard is immediate.

[01:45] Tom Reyes: what about group syncs? we want group-based roles (e.g., data-scientists => inference-operator role). can SCIM push groups?

[01:55] Jin Park: yep SCIM supports group membership mapping. we'll share a recommended mapping doc. note: group to role mapping lives in the redwood console; you can keep it in sync via SCIM.

[02:12] Laura Mitchell: moving to RBAC — we need least-privilege role templates. our baseline is separation of duties: admin, billing, deployer, read-only, security auditor. how configurable are roles?

[02:25] Jin Park: roles are very configurable. we have built-in role templates that you can clone and tweak; you can assign at org, project, and model levels. examples: read-only (view dashboard, read logs), operator (deploy/rescale), admin (manage billing and billing keys). we'll send a role matrix.

[02:45] Anika Bose: question: do you support service principals or machine users with scoped keys? we want fine-grained keys for CI pipelines.

[02:53] Samir Patel: yes, we support service principals with scoped permissions and expiry. you can mint client keys with limited scopes and rotation policies.

[03:06] Laura Mitchell: audit logs — what's contained, retention windows, and can we ship to our SIEM?

[03:14] Jin Park: audit logs include auth events, SCIM events, admin actions, API calls (token usage), and model deploy events. default retention on hosted is 90 days; enterprise customers can extend to longer retention or push logs to your S3/CloudWatch/BigQuery via a log export. we also support streaming to a customer's syslog/ELK.

[03:37] Tom Reyes: is there an immutable audit trail or are logs editable? for compliance we need tamper evidence.

[03:44] Jin Park: logs are write-once in our audit store, and exports include checksums; for high security we can integrate with append-only storage or HSM-backed signing. we'll surface the options in the doc.

[03:57] Laura Mitchell: encryption — key management, at-rest and in-transit, and bring-your-own-key (BYOK)?

[04:05] Samir Patel: all data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest we encrypt with AES-256. we have an option for customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations (BYOK) for enterprise private deployments. keys can be rotated; we can provide key rotation policies and audit records.

[04:25] Laura Mitchell: data residency — we need data for EU patients to remain in eu region. do you support region pinning?

[04:33] Jin Park: yes region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted API can pin regionally for enterprise customers; otherwise the default is US with region routing. for sensitive workloads we'd recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC peering.

[04:50] Tom Reyes: any differences in SSO/SCIM behavior between Hosted and Private?

[04:55] Jin Park: core behavior is the same; the difference is where metadata and logs live. in Private deployments your logs and SCIM flows stay inside your VPC, and you control the IdP connectivity. Hosted is simpler but audit/log export will go across the wire unless you configure private peering.

[05:15] Laura Mitchell: on RBAC least-privilege, we want examples for onboarding 50 users and a model ops team of 5. can you provide recommended policies?

[05:23] Jin Park: yes, we'll draft a role matrix: default read-only, model-deployer, infra-ops (rescale), billing-only, security-auditor (read logs and export). for model ops we suggest operator + model-edit with scoped deploy rights.

[05:40] Samir Patel: i'll also include instructions to map okta groups to these roles via SCIM, and an example SAML attribute mapping for role assertion.

[05:50] Anika Bose: question on user lifecycle: when a user is suspended in Okta, does the user get disabled immediately in Redwood? we need to ensure access revocation on first sync.

[05:58] Jin Park: yes suspend maps to inactive in SCIM. best practice: push suspend and also block token sessions; we support immediate token revocation on deprovision events.

[06:15] Laura Mitchell: auditors sometimes ask for separation of duties for billing and admin. can billing be restricted to a small finance group?

[06:23] Samir Patel: absolutely, billing is a separate permission set; you can gate that behind SSO groups and require 2FA via your IdP.

[06:34] Tom Reyes: anything special for service accounts in RBAC? how do you rotate their credentials?

[06:40] Jin Park: service principals can have short-lived tokens and automatic rotation. we recommend issuing tokens via our token service with a maximum TTL and automated rotation via CI.

[06:52] Laura Mitchell: security controls for private deployment — what network controls do you expose?

[06:58] Jin Park: in Private we support VPC peering, private endpoints, and SG rules; you can restrict egress, and we can provide IP allowlists for admin console access.

[07:12] Anika Bose: audit log retention — you said hosted default 90 days. for SOC 2 we may need 1 year. is that possible?

[07:20] Samir Patel: yes enterprise customers can set retention to 1 year or longer; otherwise we can provide a continuous export to your S3 for indefinite retention.

[07:33] Tom Reyes: compliance docs — can you share SOC 2 report and ISO27001 attestation? also do you have pen test reports?

[07:40] Samir Patel: yes we'll share bridge-letter style attestation and a limited SOC 2 report under NDA; pen test summary we can provide a public summary and full report under an MSA/processing addendum.

[07:55] Laura Mitchell: are there any known limits with SCIM group sizes or rate limits we should plan for?

[08:02] Jin Park: we have rate limits documented; typical provisioning for hundreds of thousands of users is supported in Dedicated; for Hosted we'll share the rate-limit table and recommend bulk sync patterns.

[08:18] Tom Reyes: about SAML certificates — how do you handle rotation?

[08:22] Jin Park: we support overlapping cert rotation windows; you can upload a new cert and we accept both old and new for a transition window to avoid downtime.

[08:33] Laura Mitchell: one last item — can we restrict console access by IP and also require SSO?

[08:39] Samir Patel: yes you can enforce SSO-only and add IP allowlist for admin roles; we'll include config steps.

[08:48] Jin Park: ok quick recap: we'll send SAML SP metadata + cert, SCIM provisioning guide and group mapping example, SOC 2/ISO docs under NDA, RBAC role matrix and least-privilege suggestions, and instructions for audit log exports and BYOK.

[09:06] Laura Mitchell: thanks. we'll provision a test tenant and try the SAML handshake next week. please include contact for our IdP engineer.

[09:14] Samir Patel: noted. i'll email the artifacts and schedule the RBAC workshop once you confirm availability. thanks all.

[09:22] Tom Reyes: thanks everyone.

[09:26] (call ends)
